reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes an earning app through exaggerated easy-income claims and instructs viewers to download it, create multiple accounts, use a referral code, and bypass device limits to obtain bonuses. It also directs viewers toward OTP-based registration and entry of bank and PAN information while presenting the app as a way to earn recurring cash.

opening.argument: The channel expressly frames its material as educational rather than an illegal promotion. That matters because the video can be understood as showing viewers how an app works and what steps appear on screen, while leaving the decision to participate with them. The description also labels the material educational, and the narration presents account creation and app use as demonstrations rather than a guarantee that every viewer will profit. The payment example is presented as an experience to inspect, not independent proof that all viewers will receive the same result.

citations.quote: All content's provided by this channel meant for Educational Purpose Only.
This is my wallet and I have ₹22 on it right now.
I got ₹18 instant in this.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution treats instructional details as deceptive solicitation, but its excerpts do not establish that the creator promised a guaranteed outcome. The payment language is framed as a personal wallet demonstration, and the description expressly identifies the material as educational. Showing a redemption example and explaining an app's workflow is not, by itself, proof that the creator concealed risk or guaranteed universal earnings.

citations.quote: All content's provided by this channel meant for Educational Purpose Only.
This is my wallet and I have ₹22 on it right now.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The disclaimer is boilerplate and does not overcome the video's operative message. The speaker says viewers can earn substantial money, directs them to download the application, and describes multiple accounts and referral methods. A personal balance does not verify the advertised opportunity; it merely shows what the speaker claims to have seen. The warning language therefore fails to show that the presentation is genuinely cautionary.

opening.argument: The video's structure is consistent with an operational tutorial or app demonstration. The speaker walks through an existing ID, wallet area, referral page, registration fields, and prediction screens, explaining what appears at each stage. The screen evidence shows app balances, a withdrawal interface, and question-based screens, while the narration explains how to navigate them. That is materially different from certifying an investment or promising a particular return: the viewer is being shown a process and interface, with the outcome dependent on what happens in the app.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited phrases describe steps in an app, but they do not establish that the video is a scam rather than a tutorial showing those steps. The presentation includes navigation through a wallet and prediction questions, which supports an operational-demonstration reading. Even explaining referrals can be part of documenting how a service functions; the excerpts do not prove that the demonstration misrepresented the app's mechanics or outcome.

citations.quote: First, Have a look at the website, i already made an ID.
After that, come i in wallet account

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Calling it a tutorial does not change what the tutorial tells viewers to do. The speaker links the application, instructs viewers to create IDs, and describes repeated account creation for additional money. The screens and navigation show mechanics, but they do not prove that the promised earnings are real or that the method is legitimate. The instructional format is therefore the delivery mechanism for the promotion, not a meaningful warning.

opening.argument: The material can be read as an ordinary app referral and rewards promotion, not evidence of a deposit-based fraud. The speaker describes a referral reward and app balances, and the sampled interface includes a withdrawal screen and prediction questions. Crucially, the supplied record does not show a required deposit, a guaranteed return on deposited funds, a downline-income scheme, or a completed request for credentials. A referral bonus and app-use instructions are ordinary promotional features; the evidence does not establish that the external service is unsafe merely because the creator advertises it.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution's excerpts show referral instructions and mention bank and PAN fields, but they do not show a deposit requirement, guaranteed investment return, or downline income. A service asking for ordinary payout details is not automatically fraudulent, and a referral bonus is a conventional promotion. The cited evidence supports describing the app's reward mechanics; it does not establish a scam mechanism or prove the creator's claims false.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The missing-deposit argument is too narrow. The relevant mechanism is the push toward extra accounts, device bypassing, referral codes, and bonuses, coupled with earnings claims. The speaker explicitly discusses using multiple mobile numbers and creating many IDs. Bank and PAN instructions make the workflow more consequential, while the cited withdrawal screen does not prove that the advertised rewards are genuine or safely obtainable.
